verdict.rationale: Nix documents its own isolated test environments: reproducible integration testing in virtual machines, plus dev shells and builds that only see explicitly declared dependencies. This is genuine sandbox isolation rather than a dry-run mode, but the evidence is one-line feature mentions. Nothing explicitly addresses separating test runs from production data. missing for 10: explicit documentation that test VMs/shells are isolated from production data or services, in-depth docs on the VM testing workflow, hands-on or independent corroboration of sandboxed testing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Reproducible integration testing using virtual machines.
Under Nix, a build process will only find resources that have been declared explicitly as dependencies.
`nix develop` - run a bash shell that provides the build environment of a derivation
